correctness.rationale: Complete deterministic enumeration checks every nonempty subset of each explicitly defined 16-vertex graph for connected domination, and all single-vertex replacements for selected-set sizes four, five and six. Exact BFS computes every component and all-source distances at size five. Both Python and separately written C++ sources reproduce the counts and distances; additionally, the optimum-Shrikhande-claw characterization and rook bipartite support/tree orientation argument independently explain the core structures. The result is strictly finite and does not substitute finite sampling for an infinite claim.

value.rationale: The graph pair is a canonical obstruction to uniqueness from the parameters (16,6,2,2) and common spectrum. Connected dominating sets are routing/maximum-leaf spanning tree backbones; their exact fixed-cardinality reconfiguration threshold is a natural measure of whether optimal backbones can be updated locally. The two graphs have equal optimum size but different thresholds (5 versus 6) and sharply different five-set exchange components and diameters, a distinction not implied by the scalar optimum, spectra or basic counts. This is a structural comparative finite benchmark, not an arbitrary chosen slice.
